correctness.rationale: The claim is an exact finite extremum for two explicitly defined channels. A 40-word duplication-correcting code and a 42-word deletion-correcting code give the lower bounds. The duplication upper certificate consists of 24 vertex-disjoint conflict edges plus 16 unmatched vertices, forcing an independent-set bound of 40. The deletion upper certificate partitions the graph vertices into eight conflict triangles, six conflict edges, and 28 singletons, forcing an independent-set bound of 42. The packaged verifier rebuilds the descendant relation and conflict graphs in two equivalent ways and checks every certificate block.

value.rationale: The parameter is mathematically motivated by the foundational nonequivalence examples themselves: binary source length 6 and duplication length 2 are the exact setting used to show that palindromic duplication and deletion correction differ. Computing both optima therefore sharpens a qualitative channel distinction into the exact quantitative separation 40 versus 42. The proof certificates are small and transparent, making the result a useful finite benchmark for subsequent code constructions and bounds.
